title: Partial homogenization and target denominator clearing
statement: Let $R$ and $\Lambda$ be commutative rings with an $R$-algebra structure on $\Lambda$, and let $\mathfrak q\subset\Lambda$ be a prime ideal with localization $\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Let $n,m,c\ge0$, $f_j\in R[x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m}]$, $a_i\in\Lambda$ for $1\le i\le n$, and $y_i\in\Lambda_{\mathfrak q}$ for $1\le i\le n+m$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Assume $y_i=a_i/1$ for $i\le n$ and $f_j(y)=0$ for all $j$. There are $d_j\ge0$, polynomials $F_j\in R[x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_{n+m},w]$, and values $l_0,l_1,\ldots,l_{n+m},l_w\in\Lambda$ such that: every support monomial $x^e$ of $f_j$ has extra degree $E(e)=\sum_{i>n}e_i\le d_j$; $F_j=\sum_e (f_j)_e\prod_{i=1}^{n+m}x_i^{e_i} w^{d_j-E(e)}$; $l_i=a_i$ for $i\le n$; $l_0,l_w\notin\mathfrak q$; and $l_0F_j(l_1,\ldots,l_{n+m},l_w)=0$ in $\Lambda$ for every $j$.

proof.text: Apply Mathlib IsLocalization.exist_integer_multiples_of_finite to the finite family y. This gives a common denominator w in the prime complement and numerators z_i with image w*y_i. Define b_i=a_i when i<n, and b_i=z_i otherwise. The prescribed first-coordinate hypothesis gives image(b_i)=y_i*w^(if n≤i then 1 else 0). Clearing the whole family rather than only its last m entries changes no required conclusion.

proof.text: Define d_j as Finset.sup of the extra degrees of the support; Finset.le_sup proves every degree bound, including empty support. Define F_j by the displayed monomial sum. Define the coordinate family with Fin.cases and Fin.lastCases, reserving coordinate zero for the later annihilator, inserting b in the middle, and w at the last coordinate.

proof.text: The proved private helper partial_homogenization_eval expands aeval as the finite support sum using MvPolynomial.eval₂_eq'. Factor the product of scaled variable powers using Finset.prod_mul_distrib and Finset.prod_pow_eq_pow_sum. Combine w^E with w^(d_j-E) using E≤d_j to get w^d_j for each monomial. MvPolynomial.comp_aeval_apply identifies evaluation followed by localization with evaluation of the localized coordinates. Consequently the localized evaluation of F_j is w^d_j*f_j(y)=0.

proof.text: Apply IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff to each evaluation of F_j with coordinate zero set to one, obtaining an annihilator u_j in the prime complement. Form U as the product in that submonoid, so U remains outside q, also for an empty equation family. Finset.prod_erase_mul and u_j*F_j(b,w)=0 show U annihilates each evaluation. Expanding the displayed sum shows F_j is independent of coordinate zero, so replacing that coordinate by U preserves its evaluation. Multiplicativity of aeval then proves every X_0*F_j evaluates to zero.
